# Job Chapter 35 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 429v

---

**35:1** And-answered [vaya'an] Elihu and-said: **35:2** "Do-you-reckon [chashavta] this to-be-justice [le-mishpat]? You-say, 'My-righteousness [tsidqi] [is] more-than-God's [me-El].' **35:3** For you-say, 'What does-it-profit [yiskon] you? What do-I-gain [o'il] more-than [if I had sinned] my-sin [me-chattati]?'

**35:4** I will-return [ashiv] to-you words [millin], and-to-your-friends [re'eikha] with-you. **35:5** Look [habbet] to-the-heavens [shamayim] and-see [u-re'eh]; and-behold [shur] the-clouds [shechakim] — they-are-higher [gavehu] than-you [mimekha].

**35:6** If you-sin [chata'ta], what do-you-accomplish [tif'al] against-him? And-if-your-transgressions [pesha'eikha] are-multiplied [rabbu], what do-you-do [ta'aseh] to-him? **35:7** If you-are-righteous [tsadaqta], what do-you-give [titten] to-him? Or-what from-your-hand [mi-yadkha] does-he-receive [yiqqach]?

**35:8** To-a-man [le-ish] like-you [kamokha] your-wickedness [rish'ekha] [reaches], and-to-a-son of-man [ben-adam] your-righteousness [tsidqatekha].

**35:9** From-the-multitude [me-rov] of-oppressions [ashuqim] they-cry-out [yaz'iqu]; they-call-for-help [yeshavve'u] from-the-arm [mi-zero'a] of-the-mighty [rabbim]. **35:10** And-none says [ve-lo amar], 'Where [is] God [Eloah] my-maker [osai], who-gives [noten] songs [zemirot] in-the-night [ba-lailah], **35:11** who-teaches-us [mealfenu] more-than the-beasts of-the-earth [mi-bahamot arets], and-more-than the-birds of-the-heavens [me-of ha-shamayim] makes-us-wise [yechakkemenu]?'

**35:12** There they-cry-out [yits'aqu], and-he-does-not answer [ve-lo ya'aneh], because-of the-pride [ge'on] of-the-evil [ra'im]. **35:13** Surely [akh] emptiness [shav] God [El] does-not hear [lo yishma], and-the-Almighty [Shaddai] does-not regard-it [lo yeshurenah].

**35:14** Although [af ki] you-say you-do-not behold-him [lo teshurehu], the-case [din] [is] before-him [lefanav] — and-wait [techolel] for-him. **35:15** And-now, because his-anger [appo] has-not visited [lo paqad], and-he-does-not know [lo yada] excess [pash] greatly [me'od] — **35:16** And-Iyyov opens [yiftseh] his-mouth [pihu] with-emptiness [hevel]; without knowledge [beli-da'at] words [millin] he-multiplies [yakhbir]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "My righteousness is more than God's":** Elihu's quotation (*tsidqi me-El*) may mean "my righteousness before God" or "my righteousness exceeds God's." The ambiguity is deliberate — Elihu charges Job with the stronger reading.

**v.10 — "who gives songs in the night":** Hebrew *noten zemirot ba-lailah* — a striking image. In the midst of suffering (the "night"), God gives songs. This may refer to nocturnal praise, to the instinctive worship embedded in creation, or to the revelation that comes in darkness.

**v.15 — Textual difficulty:** This verse is notoriously obscure in the Hebrew. The word *pash* is a hapax legomenon. The sense appears to be that God has not yet visited in anger, and Job does not recognize this restraint.

*— EMET*
